title: Fix bugs in daemonset controller and e2e tests

This PR is a preparation to get daemonsets working on Mesos. On the way towards this, the following bugs were found and fixed by this PR:
- the e2e tests delete all node labels. Other e2e tests might rely on them, e.g. on kubernetes.io/hostname, or in the Mesos case on some other labels.
- the pods created by the daemonset controller don't have [INLINE_CODE] set, although the code suggests it should. Hence, they are scheduled by the scheduler first, hopefully onto the right nodes. During this time, the daemonset controller thinks again and again that the nodes have no daemon pod created yet. As a consequence, it creates more and more pods until it sees the already created daemon pods scheduled to the nodes which match the selector. In the case of a slow scheduler you easily end up with tens of pods for a 2 node setup.
- the daemonset e2e test checks for resource version conflicts and tries to update again. But it does not base the update on the newest version. Hence, when the version conflict occurs, the code won't be able to fix it.

The former group (slow by necessity) need to go into their own group in perpetuity. The latter need to go into quarantine until they can be speeded up. As a first step the two groups can share one test job.

This is not just a theoretical problem. Right now, e2e tests are often timing out after 2 hours. Not long ago they completed in 30 minutes.

similar_issues.text: Don't run slow e2e tests in the parallel runs.. ref: #14206

Move remaining tests in e2e/service.go to unique namespaces.. This prevents multiple runs of the same test from trampling on each other,
both serially and in parallel. Ultimately we'll move this to a suite-wide test 
initlalization and teardown routine as per #6553, but until that's done, lets
prevent these particular tests from failing unnecessarily with this small change.

e2e tests are still busy running. I'll update this thread to confirm that they've 
succeeded.

Services e2e cleanup. Lots of misc cleanups to emit less noise during testing.

Flatten 3 tests which create load-balancers (slow) into one test.

Reduce e2e polling time in util.

Add a wait.PollImmediate() function (was a TODO) which dramatically speeds up e2e.

This test used to take 15+ minutes on my own e2e cluster and now takes less than 8 minutes.

Create fewer pods in Scheduler Predicates e2e test to speed things up.. This test was previously creating large numbers of pods (100 per node in the standard configuration), just to reserve all of the CPU resources in the cluster. This made it very slow (~8 min duration). With this PR we create a smaller number of larger pods, to speed things up.

Properly partition e2e tests with labels to avoid murkiness around what's running where. We need to make sure that at least one of our Jenkins configurations covers each e2e test. If it's never being run by automation, it is going to bit rot and we might as well not have it.

title: NegotiateVersion is not working properly
body:
NegotiateVersion has several problems:
1. NegotiateVersion does not check group/versions exposed at /apis and prints a warning message when using kubectl to create an experimental resource.
2. NegotiateVersion takes the client#Config.Version into consideration, but it's not clear what value should be put in client#Config.Version as we have multiple groups now. We plan to create a config for each group, and calls NegotiateVersion for each group.
#14592 fixes the problem but it needs to be broken into smaller pieces to receive proper review.

In #14893 we temporarily disable the warning message in NegotiateVersion. We need to revert that when we have a proper fix.

@lavalamp @krousey

### In general:

Our higher level kv abstraction is really [INLINE_CODE], so [INLINE_CODE] is only useful in the context that it provides the primitives [INLINE_CODE] needs. Having [INLINE_CODE] support base KV primitives is great, but the granularity of the [INLINE_CODE] should be matched to [INLINE_CODE] (Or generickv).
